column4: Pixel-art texture in the style of 1990s Build-engine games (Duke Nukem 3D, Blood, Redneck Rampage): a flat orthographic straight-on view filling the whole canvas edge to edge with no perspective, no background, no shadow, chunky pixels, low saturation, slightly grimy, no readable text, no logos, no border, no watermark. The wall above the bed in a guest room of a shabby Czech roadside motel from the 1970s, seen straight on: exactly the same beige wallpaper with thin brown vertical stripes as the reference, yellowed and scuffed; across the lower middle a long built-in dark veneer headboard board with a small bedside shelf at each end, a small reading lamp with a fabric shade fixed to the wall above each shelf, a cheap framed print of a mountain landscape with a faded sky hanging above the middle, a brown bakelite light switch, a damp stain spreading from the top left corner, a darker greasy patch on the wallpaper where heads leaned. No bed, no people.

The main altar of a small baroque Czech village chapel of the Virgin Mary, seen straight on and filling the canvas: a tall dark wooden retable with two twisted columns and gilded scroll ornaments with worn gold leaf, in its middle exactly the same dark old painting of the Virgin Mary in a gilded frame as the reference, a small gilded tabernacle with a little door standing on the altar table, a white lace cloth hanging over the stone altar table, two brass candlesticks with white candles, faded paper flowers in two vases, a worn stone step at the bottom. Cold grey light, old, a little damp, the same colours and grain as the reference.
